FL-002.label: Memory units have a length cap; a memory over the cap is shortened to fit as one memory, and it is split only when it holds more than one distinct fact, with the split logged.
FL-002.walk: Save an over-cap single fact: shorten it into one memory, preserving its schedule and qualifiers; split only independent claims. Repeat the scout's long single-fact and two-fact inputs three times. The same prompt repairs failed checks up to three rounds; nothing is dropped silently and the original stays in the journal (M5RM / F208).
FL-002.observed: The paid walk recalled one seeded fact. It did not submit the over-length, duplicate, rejection or secret-bearing remember cases required by this row.

FL-014.label: Every memory records the folder the agent stood in when it was made.
FL-014.walk: `/remember` while the agent stands in a folder; the card shows that folder as WHERE.
FL-014.observed: The first-prompt gate showed the selected fact before the answer. The required memory-card provenance, link or separate Injection Console gesture was not verified.

FL-017.label: Every prompt is intercepted and relevant memories are added to the context before the model runs.
FL-017.walk: Send a prompt in a thread with memories; the Injection Console shows the memories added before the model ran.
FL-017.observed: The first-prompt gate showed the selected fact before the answer. The required memory-card provenance, link or separate Injection Console gesture was not verified.

FL-018.label: A hard pause on a thread's first prompt where the user scans and removes injected memories before the model starts; afterwards removal is ad hoc with no pause.
FL-018.walk: New thread, first prompt; the gate opens with the memories and waits; the second prompt does not pause.
FL-018.observed: The first real prompt waited for Continue and then recalled the fact. A second prompt on that same memory-gated conversation was not separately verified.

FL-038.label: A cheap 80/20 duplicate check at memory creation, keeping the agent's memory work under 10% of build run time.
FL-038.walk: Save a fact already in the Palace: at cosine 0.92 or above the save comes back 'already known — reinforced' at once, between 0.80 and 0.92 it asks to confirm, without the agent reading other memories; these write-time bands are the C.4 defaults and are separate from the curator's own search band (v2.128).
FL-038.observed: The paid walk recalled one seeded fact. It did not submit the over-length, duplicate, rejection or secret-bearing remember cases required by this row.

FL-039.label: Agents make no memories until compaction; the explicit /remember command is the other way.
FL-039.walk: Run an agent thread through a turn; no memory is created mid-turn, only at compaction or by /remember. A /remember of a fact the user states is saved — checked and repaired before the Palace, never a bare refusal.
FL-039.observed: The paid walk recalled one seeded fact. It did not submit the over-length, duplicate, rejection or secret-bearing remember cases required by this row.

FL-042.label: Constitution: 'Already known — reinforced' on re-saves; rejected candidates remembered and never re-proposed without material change (gate-day).
FL-042.walk: Re-save a known fact; the reply says 'already known — reinforced'; reject a candidate and re-save it unchanged; it is not proposed again.
FL-042.observed: The paid walk recalled one seeded fact. It did not submit the over-length, duplicate, rejection or secret-bearing remember cases required by this row.

FL-044.label: At compaction the summarizing agent turns anything important but not needed for the next few build steps into a memory through the normal memory creation path, and compaction waits for those memories to land before dropping the rest.
FL-044.walk: Cross a compaction on a main thread: every fact a continuing agent would want lands as its own self-contained memory (no count cap; shorten one over-long claim, split only independent claims), a curator pass follows and merges them with what the Palace already holds, the last share of the conversation is still there word for word, the next prompt's injection can draw on the new facts, and the whole original chat is still on record beside the facts drawn from it (owner, 2026-10-05, v2.133; M5RM).
FL-044.observed: A real manual compaction reduced 5,476 tokens to 166 and produced candidates. It did not establish every fact’s provenance, automatic fill-line handling, or the interactive planning path.

FL-207.label: A workflow is a folder — the bundle: its recipe, its skills, its tools and the names of its keys — that checks, packs to one archive with a digest, and saves as a job carrying that digest.
FL-207.walk: `nocturne workflow new <folder>` makes the folder. Add a SKILL.md folder under .agents/skills, an executable under tools, a key name in keys.example and a cron line in workflow.json. `nocturne workflow check <folder>` refuses until the vault holds the named key, then lists the tool with its --help line, the key name and the digest. `nocturne workflow pack <folder>` from two different folders writes the same .tar bytes, whose sha256 is the digest. `nocturne jobs save <folder>` records the digest on the job; the Jobs module's row reads 'bundle <digest head>' and its detail shows the digest, the tools and the key names (names only). The run's tool inventory lists the bundle's skill.
FL-207.observed: Workflow unit and contract tests ran. The model-setting walk did not run a saved bundle, wait for its schedule, or observe its job dashboard on the paid Palace.

FL-209.label: A tool runs with its keys and the agent never sees them: `nocturne tool run <name>` executes the bundle's own code with the vault's variables; in a saved job that is not a boundary crossing, and the walls a recipe declares are crossed unattended once the owner confirmed them at save.
